title: Organic food not more nutritious says study
summary: TV interview with a dietitian on the 2012 Stanford study: organic is not more nutritious but has fewer residues and resistant bacteria.

assertions.quote: perhaps organic vegetables don't have more vitamin C

verdicts.note: Organic crops had more antioxidants and vitamin C but less protein (-15%), amino acids, fibre and vitamin E, and no difference for most minerals, so the gain is in some compounds, not nutrition across the board.

Systematic review of 223 food-composition studies (abstract only): estimates were highly heterogeneous, only phosphorus differed and not meaningfully, and the literature lacks strong evidence organic food is more nutritious.
AAP clinical report (abstract only): current evidence does not support any meaningful nutritional benefits or deficits from eating organic.
Organic milk had higher alpha-tocopherol (+13%) and iron (+20%) and better fatty acids, but 74% less iodine and 21% less selenium, so it is not uniformly more nutritious.
Organic meat showed higher PUFA and n-3 but the evidence on minerals, antioxidants and vitamins was too thin for meta-analysis, so the advantage is shown only for fat profile.

Crop vitamins and minerals are similar under both systems; organic has modestly more phenolics and its dairy about 50% more omega-3, but the review calls established nutritional differences small with no strong health conclusions.
Clark and Tilman cite reviews finding higher micronutrient concentrations in organic foods but note the differences may not translate into improved health outcomes; a passing citation.

assertions.quote: the organic produce had about 30% fewer pesticide residues
they had less of the res antibiotic resistance res istent bacteria

verdicts.note: Systematic review (abstract only): risk of isolating bacteria resistant to 3+ antibiotics was 33 percentage points higher in conventional than organic chicken and pork.

Organic pork and chicken are less likely to harbour resistant bacteria, resistance is less common in organic pigs in four countries, and converting poultry farms to organic cut resistant Salmonella; MRSA differences lost significance after adjustment.

assertions.quote: we don't really have the data to to know that yet

verdicts.note: Systematic review of 35 studies: observational links (lower NHL, metabolic syndrome, pre-eclampsia etc.) are confounded by healthier diets and lifestyles, trials are short with surrogate markers, and evidence does not allow a definitive statement of benefit.

Systematic review (abstract only): only 3 of 17 human studies examined clinical outcomes and found no differences for allergy or Campylobacter, and adult biomarker studies found no clinically meaningful differences.
AAP clinical report (abstract only): no well-powered human studies directly demonstrate health benefits or disease protection from an organic diet.

Authors say health impacts of organic milk must be extrapolated from composition because virtually no studies assessed organic food consumption against health outcomes; only suggestive cohort links (eczema, hypospadias) exist.
Authors state there are so far no cohort studies linking organic meat consumption to reduced eczema or other positive health outcomes.

The review concludes the link between organic food and health is insufficiently documented and that it is not possible to tell whether organic food plays a causal role in observed lower allergy, obesity or NHL, given residual confounding.
A risk model, not an outcome study, found no measurable health benefit from swapping to organic Dirty Dozen produce via pesticide exposure; other pathways not assessed.

assertions.quote: it's pricier it can be a lot pricier

verdicts.note: AAP clinical report (abstract only): organic foods regularly command a significant price premium.
The authors state that organic foods remain less affordable than conventional equivalents and that high prices are a major obstacle to buying them; asserted, not measured.

Hedonic model on 2004-10 Nielsen Homescan purchases, controlling for package, brand, store and market, found positive organic premiums for all 17 products, above 20% for 16 of them (2010: 7% spinach to 82% eggs); meat and poultry were not covered.

In French supermarket shelf prices recorded weekly by the official RNM network (2016-17), every organic fruit and vegetable was significantly dearer than its conventional version, 98% on average (peaches +151%), and a household's annual organic basket cost 660 EUR against 368 EUR (+79%).

US wholesale and farmgate premiums for organic broccoli and carrots were close to or above 100% in 2000-04, but organic mesclun mix carried only a 6-9% wholesale premium, so the gap varies widely by product; wholesale and farm prices only, three commodities.

assertions.quote: if you can't afford organic you should still be buying your fruits and vegetables
you can go to the environmental working group online and it shows you which uh fruits and vegetables have more pesticides or less

verdicts.note: The ranking sums normalized residue frequency, number, concentration and (since 2025) a NOAEL-based toxicity ratio, so it ranks measured residue load, but it weights nothing by how much of each food people eat and compares nothing to a health threshold.

The 2010 EWG method ignored food consumption and toxicological thresholds and was skewed toward counts of multiple residues, so it could not rank risk (blueberries, cherries and kale had all exposures over 30,000-fold below RfDs); EWG has since added a toxicity factor but still no consumption weighting.
